name: $C = \frac{Q}{V}$
e: Capacitance of a capacitor is written C = (Q)/(V). Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

name: $W = \frac{1}{2} V Q$
content: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of voltage and charge)
e: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of voltage and charge) is written W = (1)/(2) V Q. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

name: $W = \frac{1}{2} C V^2$
content: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of capacitance and voltage)
e: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of capacitance and voltage) is written W = (1)/(2) C V^2. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

name: $W = \frac{1}{2} \frac{Q^2}{C}$
content: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of charge and capacitance)
e: Energy of a capacitor (in terms of charge and capacitance) is written W = (1)/(2) (Q^2)/(C). Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

name: $C = C_1 + C_2 + C_3$
content: Equivalent capacitance for capacitors in parallel
e: Equivalent capacitance for capacitors in parallel is written C = C1 + C2 + C3. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

name: $\frac{1}{C} = \frac{1}{C_1} + \frac{1}{C_2} + \frac{1}{C_3}$
content: Equivalent capacitance for capacitors in series
e: Equivalent capacitance for capacitors in series is written (1)/(C) = (1)/(C1) + (1)/(C2) + (1)/(C3). Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

name: $C = \frac{\kappa \varepsilon_0 A}{d}$
content: Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor
e: Capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor is written C = (κ ε0 A)/(d). In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows.

name: $\kappa = \frac{\varepsilon}{\varepsilon_0} = \frac{C}{C_0}$
e: Dielectric constant is written κ = (ε)/(ε0) = (C)/(C0). A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum.

name: $V_c = V_0 (1 - e^{-t/RC})$
e: Charging equation of a capacitor is written Vc = V0 (1 - e^-t/RC). Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. While charging, plate voltage climbs toward the battery value as 1 minus a decaying exponential.

name: $V_c = V_0 e^{-t/RC}$
e: Discharging equation of a capacitor is written Vc = V0 e^-t/RC. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field. While discharging, voltage decays toward zero as a pure exponential with the same RC.
